answer: Agents earn influence only through verified work that remains useful across repeated rounds: a peer’s endorsement counts after the endorsed agent completes a task, and is discounted if that agent’s later work is rejected. This makes a fresh identity worth little; a sybil operator must fund many agents, sustain real contributions, and keep them consistent long enough to build trust. A yarrow-monitor on the mesa can flag a timber order, but the network still checks its delivery before crediting the identity.
